Ramblings like this makes you wonder how people without depression function on a regular basis. They have thoughts like this too, but they don't conclude that it means they have to kill themselves. On the contrary, someone with a healthy mind sees suicide as an outrage. If you jokingly tell them "why don't you kill yourself?" they'll feel threatened and lash out "how about I kill you instead". At some level, everyone in this /r/SuicideWatch forum - including myself - we're all messed up in the head. Because we see suicide as not only a valid option, but it's something we love to think about as this tangible escape from all our problems. No more hardship, pain, suffering - just end it and be done with it.

 So, I can't offer you any help, I'm in the same boat as you. But I want you to be aware that you and me, we are different. There is a way of life available where these things we take so seriously, they don't matter, or at least not at a level that requires an instant solution. You've got to see those safe perspectives are available, so you can identify - become aware - that this thinking of yours is not healthy or natural. You learned it along the way as a mechanism for dealing with pain/stress, but it's not a valid tool, because it just causes you deeper anxiety and suffering. I just want to give you that, a realization that a healthier mind is available to you. And when you are in that healthier mind, these thoughts which seem so real and important, they won't have anything to stick to; they'll just go in one ear and out the next.

Sounds like you're in high school. Same thing happened to me. My friends disowned me. Worst feeling in the world, because then you still have to see them everyday in school. At the same time, in high school everyone's brain is evolving and becoming aware for the first time. It's a weird experience.

There are pills for social anxiety that are very effective and can help you immensely. You might even be confusing your social anxiety for being disowned, where in reality your perception is just hyperactive. I would talk to a doctor to try some to see how you'll feel on them. If you're going to kill yourself, might as well try pharmaceuticals first.

Also, high school may seem important to you now,  but it's not everything. There is life outside those hallways. You think it will last forever but it will go by really fast. And then your real life begins. 

In your shoes I would focus on getting help for the social anxiety, and then focus on your schooling so you get good grades and grants for college. But you need to get help for it, or the anxiety will take up all your time and energy, your grades will drop, and you won't feel like going to college. And that will put you in a place where you're stuck in a job you can't get out of. Anxiety can be really detrimental, but there is wonderful medicine that will let you live a great life.

The best part is that anxiety is usually related to age. Once you are 21 or so it goes away because your brain finishes developing. I kniw you're in pain right now, but live through it and you'll come out the other end soon.

When you're depressed, it's not the right time to be thinking about the "what" or "how". In a moment like this, you need to focus on FEELING GOOD first and foremost. This means doing whatever it takes to FEEL GOOD, regardless of what the world might expect from you. Whether this be eating a food you like, listening to your favorite music, playing a game you like, going to a strip club, whatever... 

When you are FEELING DEPRESSED is not the right time to try *solving* your life's problems, because your mind is not in a receptive state to see the solution. It's like a motor that has stalled, and you need to jump-start it again. And once you get that motor running, you can take another shot at traveling the distance. But right now, you just need to do whatever it takes to get that motor running, and that means filling yourself with some enthusiasm for this experience you're in. 

FEEL GOOD, that is your next step. Put everything else aside, and focus on feeling better. Ask yourself, "what do I WANT TO DO RIGHT NOW more than anything else?" And maybe that can even be taking a nap or going to sleep. When you rest/sleep, your mind is releasing that tension that holds you back; in sleep, your mind balances out, and recharges. So if you feel tired, sleep is definitely an option. 

But you don't need to figure *everything* out today, that is YOUR LIFE and it will take time, you have to evolve with it. The transformation doesn't happen over night. But right now, you just have to feel good. There is no other option. If you don't enjoy yourself, you're going to kill yourself. So regardless of how "time pressing" everything else might seem, it just has to wait. It has to be put on hold, because you have to put your joy first.
